abstract.t: The Mail Action Protocol (MAP) defines how a service describes an action in email, how a client requests that action over HTTPS, and how the service reports and retains the result. A request is bound to the exact description by its digest. A request is authorized either by the client's existing service credential or, for operations whose contract permits it, by a capability the message itself carries. MAP reuses the JSON-LD representation and MIME structure of the Structured Email work. Interaction types are defined by digest-bound contracts, so adding a type does not change this protocol. MAP does not replace email transport or define an agent identity system.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Email routinely asks a recipient to act in another service: approve terms, supply information, respond to an event, confirm an address or change a preference. A person can interpret the message and follow a link. An automated client needs more: a stable description of the operation, the exact object and terms on which it acts, the authority the action rests on, what completing it gives away, and the possible outcomes.

MAP defines that interaction without moving business authority into email. The service remains authoritative for identity, permission, target state, approvals and the operation's effect. The readable email and normal service interface remain available to a person.
The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, and MAY in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

section.name: Scope and Relationship to Existing Work
section.t: MAP descriptions are JSON-LD documents carried in an application/ld+json MIME part designated by Structured Email . SMTP, Internet Message Format, MIME, mailbox access and provider APIs continue to perform their existing roles .

MAP 0.2 uses HTTPS, the service's existing authentication, and existing email authentication . It defines no custom DNS record, new media type, global identity provider, mandatory online registry lookup or general permission-policy language. Its authority for message-carried actions follows the pattern of one-click unsubscribe .

dl.dd: The authority that owns an operation, checks permission, performs the effect and records its result.
An agent, inbox or application that reads a description and may submit a request on behalf of a principal.
A versioned contract defining the details, operations, inputs, results, authority and consequences of a class of interaction.
Type-defined data in a description, such as terms to approve, fields to complete or times on offer.
The SHA-256 digest of the canonical form of a description, which binds a request to it.
An unguessable value in a service URL that authorizes the operations one message offers, for one recipient.
What completing an operation gives away: refusal, protection, record, disclosure, commitment, authorization or assertion.
A service interface through which a person can inspect and complete the interaction.

section.name: Structured Email Representation
section.t: A description is a Structured Email partial representation . The service MUST carry it in an application/ld+json part labelled with the profile through the media type's profile parameter , as application/ld+json; profile="https://mailschema.org/profiles/map/0.2". The part MUST carry Content-Purpose: Machine-readable, use base64 or quoted-printable content-transfer encoding, and sit in a multipart/related entity beside the readable content. That entity is the message body or one of its parts, as when the message also carries attachments. Other structured parts, including descriptions labelled with other profiles, may sit beside it.

A client MUST consider only parts outside any attached message. It processes the one designated part whose profile parameter lists the profile it implements, ignores every other structured part, and refuses the message when more than one part carries that label or the part is not in a multipart/related entity with readable content. It never infers a description from an undesignated attachment.

Every MAP document is I-JSON : valid UTF-8 without a byte order mark, no duplicate member names, no lone surrogates or noncharacters (U+FDD0 to U+FDEF, and the last two code points of every plane), and every number, read as the nearest IEEE 754 double, within plus or minus 2^53-1. No string or member name contains U+0000 either, which many stores refuse or truncate. Every MAP document is at most 64 KiB, and its arrays and objects nest at most 32 deep, the outermost counting as one.

Lexical forms are the core schema's patterns: date-times, dates, URIs, HTTPS URLs and origins, the result template and email addresses. A validator MUST NOT assert the JSON Schema format keyword, since format checkers differ between implementations. Every pattern is printable ASCII in a subset that ECMA-262 with the u flag and other regular expression engines read alike. Any other code point is written as \uXXXX, and the only escapes are an escaped syntax character, \t, \n, \f, \r, \uXXXX outside the surrogates and, within a class, \-. A pattern uses only literal and escaped characters; non-empty character classes, with a hyphen only in a range or at either end and no bracket or &&; (?: groups; alternation; ^ and $; and one *, +, ?, {n}, {n,} or {n,m} quantifier after an atom, with bounds of at most four digits and n no greater than m. ^ and $ anchor the start and end of the whole value, as in ECMA-262; an engine whose $ also matches before a final newline, or whose anchors match at line breaks, MUST read them as absolute anchors. Every multipleOf is an integer.

Implementations bundle the exact artifacts the profile record binds, and MUST NOT resolve a schema or context named by a message. JSON-LD expansion is optional; an implementation that expands a description uses the bundled profile context. Extraction and validation MUST NOT execute an operation or grant authority.

section.name: Description
section.t: The MAP 0.2 profile URI is https://mailschema.org/profiles/map/0.2, and a client MUST match it exactly. The profile record, published at https://mailschema.org/profiles/map/0.2.json, binds three artifacts by the SHA-256 digest of their exact bytes, which implementations bundle:

dl.dd: https://mailschema.org/schemas/map-0.2.schema.json, SHA-256 732d60fcb758d945dc15c57d885c9d1c0c76423a7439096d9755e8ec9830836a.
https://mailschema.org/contexts/map-0.2.jsonld, SHA-256 dfed0189524d7d16d31ed3d8af97e9a0c458200c4c034b413f9d14fa35b60257.
https://mailschema.org/schemas/type-contract-0.2.schema.json, SHA-256 e030007cc034662c9d9d448a8a035aff3106cfb96fb60e6aa9f92b99b25df0b9.

section.t: The principal members of a description, in the JSON data model , are:

dl.dd: A UUID URN identifying the interaction.
The interaction type URI, version and contract digest.
When the interaction was described and when it expires, which is later.

The service identity, its authority mode, the protected resource identifier for credential authority, the HTTPS execution URL without a fragment, a result URL template containing {requestId} once and outside any fragment, a result retention interval from 300 seconds to one year, and the human route. Under credential authority it may name, as onBehalfOf, the party the service asks for when that is not the service itself: an id URI that identifies the party at the service, the same in all its interactions, and the name the service shows.

For possession authority, the address the capability was issued to. Its local part may be internationalized , without spaces or invisible and bidirectional format characters; its domain is written as A-labels.
The service object, its revision and a service-issued SHA-256 digest. The revision and digest cover only terms the service controls, never responses to the interaction.
Present exactly when the type contract defines them. Numbers are integers, and member names are ASCII identifiers: a letter, then at most 63 letters, digits or underscores.
Offered operation identifiers with readable labels, each offered at most once.

section.t: Before acting, a client MUST validate the description against the core schema, match its profile, select the bundled contract its type names and compare the contract digest, validate the details against that contract, check that each offered operation permits the authority mode, and refuse a description whose expiry has passed. It prepares one request for each instruction of its principal, validates its input against the request schema and every field binding, and reuses that request, with its identifier, when the same instruction is carried out again, as on redelivery.

A description is immutable. A changed contract, target revision, details or operation set is a new interaction with a new identifier, and a service that delivers the same interaction again MUST send the same description. The description MUST NOT contain an access token, session credential or grant, other than a possession capability in its execution route.

section.name: Description Digest
section.t: The description digest is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the description serialized with the JSON Canonicalization Scheme , exactly as parsed from the message, prefixed with sha-256:. The service computes it over the description it serializes into the message, which a client parses back to the same canonical form. It stores the digest with the interaction, or rebuilds the identical description from the interaction identifier and state that cannot change; a rebuilt description whose content would differ is a different interaction. Every request carries the digest. The service MUST refuse a request whose digest differs from that of the description it issued, without claiming its request identifier.
The digest binds everything a client was shown, including terms, wording and links. A forged message that reuses a genuine interaction identifier cannot produce an accepted request.

section.name: Authority
section.t: Each operation in a type contract declares the authority it permits. An interaction has one mode, and every operation it offers MUST permit that mode.

section.name: Credential Authority
section.t: The client holds an existing credential for the service, sent only in the Authorization header. Before using it, the client MUST match the service identity, exact HTTPS execution URL, result URL template and resource against configuration obtained independently of the email, and MUST apply the same checks to every redirect. The human route MUST sit under the resource's organizational domain. Message authentication alone is insufficient.

A client MAY obtain that configuration from OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata for a resource identifier it already trusts. The map_services metadata parameter lists the MAP services at the resource: each entry has an id, the implemented profiles, an exact execution_url and an exact result_url_template, both of which MUST use HTTPS on the resource identifier's origin. Nothing in an email selects the resource.

Authentication establishes the principal, on whose behalf a request is made, and the actor that sent it, such as an OAuth client, the actor of a delegated token , an API key, or a client authenticated with HTTP Message Signatures . The service MUST record the actor of each claimed request and human decision separately from the principal.

The party asking is the service, or the party it names in onBehalfOf, for which it vouches. The client MUST present that party with the service and key its principal's policy to the service identifier and the party's id together, never to a name.

section.name: Possession Authority
section.t: The message is the authority for the operations it offers on its target. The service MUST:

ul.li: issue one capability per interaction and recipient: at least 128 bits from a cryptographically secure generator, written as at least 22 base64url characters without padding , as the last segment of the execution URL path;
use HTTPS, never redirect, and never require cookies or HTTP authentication;

answer an unknown capability with a plain 404 and a lapsed one with 410. A capability lapses once the interaction has expired, its retention interval has passed, measured from its expiry, and no result of a request claimed before expiry is still retained. A refusal recorded after expiry never extends it. Once lapsed, the plain 410 replaces every MAP answer under the capability;

sign the message with a DKIM signature aligned with the From domain, using rsa-sha256 with a key of at least 2048 bits or ed25519-sha256 , without an l= tag, and covering From, To, Date, Message-ID, MIME-Version and Content-Type, and Cc, List-Id and OTP-Token whenever the message carries them;
when sending for customers, send only under the customer's own verified, aligned domain.

section.t: Before any possession request, the client MUST establish all of the following:

ul.li: The message carries such a signature, which the client verified on the raw message. The signature is currently valid, its algorithm matches the published key, and it is aligned under the DMARC policy of the From domain or its organizational domain. The client reads header fields as its DKIM verifier reads them and refuses a malformed field. The message carries each signed header, and Subject, at most once, its From header names exactly one mailbox, and its Date is a valid section 3.3 date-time with a numeric zone, a year from 1900 and none of the obsolete forms. An SPF-only DMARC pass, a pass obtained through ARC or a local override, and authentication results from any system other than the client's own receiving system do not count.

The execution URL, result template, human route and service identifier sit under the From domain's organizational domain, as the RFC 9989 DNS tree walk determines it, compared as A-labels . A DNS failure other than a definite absence, or an organizational domain that is a top-level domain, refuses the message.

The recipient is an address the principal controls, and the message was sent to it. Addresses are compared with their ASCII letters in lowercase, every other character exactly, and their domains as A-labels.

section.t: The client MUST send no credentials and MUST treat a redirect as a failure. Anyone who receives a forwarded copy holds the same authority, so a contract permits possession only where that is acceptable. Under possession authority the capability is the principal, results never name an actor, and the client presents the From organizational domain, not the service name, as the party asking.

section.name: Consequences
section.t: Every operation declares one or more consequences, so a client can apply its principal's policy to a type it has not implemented. Refusal and protection stand alone. Under possession authority, a client MUST NOT complete an operation whose consequences go beyond refusal, protection and record without a prior relationship between the principal and the sending organization, or the principal's decision. A client without a type's own rule treats an assertion as needing the principal's decision. A disclosure sends the principal's information to the service and through it to any party it asks for. When it asks a person to decide, the client shows the party asking, the details and the target, not the readable body.

section.name: Requests and Results
section.t: The client sends a POST using HTTP semantics with Content-Type: application/json to the execution URL. The request carries the profile, a client-generated requestId, the interaction identifier, the description digest, the type reference, the operation and its input, and MUST validate against the core schema and the contract's request schema. The service MUST answer another method on the execution URL with 405 and Allow: POST, and MUST answer 415 unless the media type is application/json, compared case-insensitively, with no parameter other than charset=utf-8; empty parameter slots, which HTTP permits, are ignored.

A service answers in three stages, and nothing answered in the first two is claimed. First the HTTP binding, before the body is read, in any order: another method with 405, another media type with 415, a URL that names no result resource with a plain 404, a missing credential with authentication-required, and under possession authority an unknown capability with a plain 404 and a lapsed one with a plain 410. Then, with an uncorrelated invalid-request, a malformed request, an unknown interaction and a request whose digest differs from the description it issued. Then, in any order that applies no effect for a problem and reveals no protected state, the principal's current permission, the profile, type, operation and authority, expiry, a decided interaction, staleness against its own state, and the input, field bindings and type rules.

Results use application/json. The state is accepted, completed or failed with status 200, or pending or approval-required with status 202 and a Retry-After header. A failed result carries a reason. An approval-required result carries an approval URL, which shows the proposal's input and the terms the description digest binds. A GET on the approval URL or the human route MUST be side-effect free, since link scanners follow links in mail, and any change a person makes there MUST take their deliberate action, protected from cross-site requests. Under credential authority, a result may name the requesting actor with an opaque reference, which stays the same across transitions and is never an identity claim.

Every operation is a decision unless its contract marks it repeatable. The first decision whose result reaches its operation's success state, accepted or completed, decides the interaction. A decision whose result is pending holds the interaction while the service carries it out: it decides the interaction if it succeeds and leaves it undecided if it fails. A decision request made while the interaction is decided or held is refused as already-decided, and any decision still awaiting approval when the interaction is decided ends as failed with reason superseded. Repeatable operations, and approvals of them, remain available until the interaction expires. The service authorizes a human decision independently of the proposal. An unauthorized decision attempt, or one the service's rules refuse at that moment, is answered with refused and leaves the proposal unchanged. An operation that can require approval MUST declare the failure reasons declined, stale-target and expired, and a decision also superseded. An undecided approval fails with reason expired at the interaction's expiry.

Problems use application/problem+json . A problem's type is https://mailschema.org/problems/ followed by its code, and its type, HTTP status and code member MUST agree as the following table gives. A problem is correlated, carrying the profile, the request identifier, the interaction identifier when the service knows it, the code, and the result URL as its instance, only when it states what happened to a request: a claimed request's recorded response, or an idempotency-conflict, request-in-progress, result-not-found or expired-interaction for its identifier. A refusal of the caller's access to a claimed request, on a retry, a read or a decision, says nothing about the request, so it is not correlated and changes nothing. Neither is a problem for an unclaimed request, nor an authentication-required problem. Only invalid-request, refused and authentication-required are ever uncorrelated.

tr.td: Correct the request. Malformed, unknown-interaction and unknown-description requests are not claimed.
The caller may not perform the operation or read the result.
No retained result exists for the caller.
The target changed; the problem carries the current target.
The identifier belongs to another request value.
The identifier is claimed without a result yet.
Another request decided the interaction, or holds it while its decision is carried out.
The interaction, or its retained result, has expired.
The exact type is not implemented.
The operation was not offered or implemented.

section.t: The service answers input that fails the operation's request schema, a field binding or a type rule with a claimed invalid-request. Its errors are JSON Pointers into the input; implementations may list different errors for the same input, but agree on the verdict. A service MUST NOT apply the requested effect when returning a problem.

section.name: Idempotency and Recovery
section.t: A claimed requestId identifies one complete request value within the service's tenant: under credential authority, the account the service scopes the principal to; under possession authority, the capability. Each tenant has its own identifiers. An exact retry by the principal that claimed the identifier returns the latest recorded response without applying the effect again, after current authorization is rechecked. Reuse with a changed value is an idempotency-conflict. Use of the identifier by another principal in the tenant is refused without disclosing the saved response. A client SHOULD make request identifiers unpredictable, as random UUIDv4 and UUIDv7 values are , since another principal in the tenant who predicts one could claim it first. The identifier travels in the body rather than in an Idempotency-Key header , because it also names the result resource.

Malformed requests, and requests for an unknown interaction or description, MUST NOT claim their identifier, so the service refuses them before any check that could claim it. For every other request, claiming the identifier, applying or durably initiating the effect, and recording recoverable state MUST be atomic, or the service MUST reconcile an interrupted operation without repeating it.

The result URL is the result URL template with {requestId} replaced by the request identifier, each : written as %3A. The service returns it in a Location header. A side-effect-free GET there by the principal that made the request returns the latest recorded result or problem, after current permission is rechecked. A URL whose place for the identifier holds anything but a request identifier is not a result resource, and the service answers it with a plain 404, whatever credential comes with it; a request target that is not well-formed may instead get HTTP's own 400. After a timeout, a client SHOULD read the result before any request that might repeat the effect. Results remain available until the later of the interaction's expiry and the retention interval measured from the latest recorded state. Duplicate suppression outlives them.

A service MAY delete an interaction with its target, as when the target's owner deletes it. It then answers a request for the interaction as for an unknown interaction, and a read of any of its results as result-not-found; nothing is applied again, because the target is gone.

section.name: Interaction Types
section.t: A type contract defines its target, details, and each operation's authority, consequences, repeatability, inputs, results and failure reasons. Each operation declares exactly one success state, accepted or completed. An operation that permits possession never declares approval-required, and one that declares pending declares how it fails. Only an operation that declares approval-required uses the reserved reasons declined, stale-target and expired. A decision among them also declares superseded, and only such a decision uses it. The request schema extends the core request, binds the type identifier and version, and has one branch for each operation of the contract and no other. A field binding ties an input to a form fields block in the details: the input then carries only the fields the details define, and satisfies each, including required fields and each field's lexical form; where the details define no fields block for a binding, its input is absent.

The Registry compiles every contract schema strictly. Every keyword belongs to a JSON Schema 2020-12 vocabulary; the one annotation beyond them, autocomplete, belongs to the form fields block. A type names one type. A keyword that constrains one JSON type has that type declared in the same schema or in an enclosing one that applies to the same value through allOf, anyOf, oneOf, not, if, then, else or dependentSchemas. No keyword is left without effect: if has then or else, then and else have if, and minContains and maxContains have contains. prefixItems with n schemas sets minItems to n, and items to false or maxItems to n. Every $ref is a pinned URL with an empty fragment or a plain JSON Pointer to a schema, and only the request schema's root declares $id and $schema, which is JSON Schema 2020-12. Contract schemas never use an anchor or a dynamic reference. A contract pins, by digest, every schema it depends on. A description binds the type URI, version and SHA-256 digest of the contract serialized with the JSON Canonicalization Scheme . Implementations do not guess compatibility. Adding a type does not change this protocol.
A Registry record adds discovery metadata, maintainers, examples, evidence and history without changing the wire contract. Registry lookup is not required during an interaction.
Ten types are published with MAP 0.2:

ul.li: Content Review;
Action Approval, whose terms follow the authorization details of ;
Information Request;
Event Response, a binding of iTIP replies;
Meeting Scheduling;
Subscription Preferences, which leaves unsubscribing to ;
Task Assignment;
Payment Request;
Email Confirmation;
Account Activity.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Implementations treat structured content as attacker-controlled. The credential checks in prevent an email from redirecting a service credential. The description digest prevents a forged or altered description from being acted on. Schema validation establishes neither trust nor permission.
Possession authority transfers with every copy of a message. The rules in limit it as follows:

ul.li: recipient binding stops replay to other recipients;
strict DKIM verification stops forgery and appended content;
the organizational domain rule stops redirection to another organization;
consequences, and type rules such as confirming only a request the client recorded, stop assertions a principal did not make.

section.t: A lookalike domain can pass authentication; it cannot satisfy a recorded-request rule. The rules in keep capabilities out of logs, referrers and human routes.

Services protect result resources with current authorization and disclose no token, private content or permission information beyond what the caller may know. A service can grant a caller no authority, proposal authority that produces approval-required, or delegated authority that can produce completed. MAP does not infer authority from whether the caller is automated.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Descriptions travel through email systems and may be retained or forwarded. They should carry the minimum details needed to act, and sensitive material should stay behind an authorized service route. Form fields cannot request passwords, one-time codes or payment card data. Results should not be retained longer than the service's stated purpose requires.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: MAP uses existing media types, HTTPS and the existing OAuth protected resource metadata document. It requests no new media type or well-known URI.
IANA is requested to register the following parameter in the "OAuth Protected Resource Metadata" registry established by :

section.name: Implementation Status
section.t: This section follows and may be removed before publication as an RFC.

The MailSchema repository at publishes MAP 0.2's digest-bound schemas and ten type contracts. It also publishes a contract-driven reference service and client, and a conformance suite of 99 cases mapped to 38 requirements. The suite includes DKIM-signed genuine and forged messages and shared RFC 8785, I-JSON, lexical and media type vectors, which a Ruby implementation also passes.

Nitrosend completed a provider-delivered Content Review exchange on MAP 0.1, the withdrawn predecessor of this document. No independent implementation is claimed, and MailSchema and Nitrosend share ownership.
